blocks.text: *Gear that shapes your kit, your defense, and your look.*
Weapons decide your skills

Your weapon is more than a stat stick — it **grants the active skills** on your hotbar (see *Skills*). Every weapon is a real 3D object your character holds, and swapping weapons swaps your whole kit.
The weapon roster

Every weapon owns a **distinct playstyle** — one clear reason to wield it. That playstyle isn't a design label: each of the twelve is the last surviving trace of one of the **Twelve Unwritten**, and how the weapon fights *is* how that person fought. None of them was ever named — only described by the deed witnesses remembered. They fall into three families:
Might — physical power, up close

blocks.text: Each weapon type has a deep pool of skills, and **every weapon that drops rolls its own kit** from that pool — which skills surface is pure chance, so no two of the same weapon play exactly alike. You can then shape it further at the forge. See *Skills* for how kits roll, and *Crafting & Recycling* for reforging, refining, transmog, and turning unwanted weapons into Essence.

blocks.text: Each piece adds stats and defense; some carry set flavor or elemental properties.
Refinement (+N)
Gear can be **refined** to higher plus-levels:

items: A **weapon** gains **+3 Attack per refine level**.
**Every** piece of gear gains **+1 Defense per refine level**.

blocks.text: So a +10 weapon is +30 Attack over its base, and any +10 piece is +10 Defense.
Rarity

Gear comes in rarity tiers — **Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary** — rolled for each copy as it drops, and shown by its border color. On a weapon, rarity makes its skills and its own attack hit harder. On a piece of armour, it raises the piece's defence or magic defence by the same ladder and adds a flat extra to every main stat the piece rolled. Rarity does **not** decide which skills a weapon carries, how many of them, or whether it gets an ultimate: every weapon rolls the same kind of kit whatever its tier.

**And a rarer weapon hits harder.** Every skill it grants is lifted by its tier — **+3** on an Uncommon, **+9** Rare, **+18** Epic, **+30** Legendary. Those are points added to how much your Ring already multiplies that skill, so early on a Legendary is about a third more damage, and as your Ring grows the same 30 points become a smaller slice of a bigger number. Either way a Legendary is worth the same to you as to anyone else. It lifts damage, healing, shield size, damage-over-time, how far a buff or debuff moves your stats, and what one Opening-style charge is worth. It never makes a stun, a freeze or any other timer last longer, and it never changes how often something procs. Two swords with the same skills are not the same sword.

blocks.text: How many skills a weapon rolls

Every weapon rolls the same way, whatever its rarity: **3 or 4 actives**, **3 or 4 passives**, and a **1-in-4 chance** of an **Ultimate** on top. The two halves are rolled separately, so 3 actives with 4 passives is just as likely as 4 and 4.

rows: 9 — a full kit with its Ultimate

blocks.text: So **seven skills is typical**, and about **one weapon in sixteen** drops with the full nine. Only the **Sword**'s skill pool is finished today — every other weapon type currently drops with no skills at all until its pool is written.
Cards
Some gear has **card slots** you can socket with cards for monster-matchup bonuses. See **Cards**.
